claim: For the standard \(d\)-dimensional quantum erasure channel \(\mathcal E_{p,d}\), \[\mathcal E_{p,d}(\rho)=(1-p)\rho\oplus p\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)|e\rangle\langle e|,\qquad d\ge2,\] and Sutter--Scholz--Winter--Renner approximate-degradability parameter \(\varepsilon_{\mathcal E_{p,d}}=\inf_{\Xi}\|\mathcal E^c_{p,d}-\Xi\circ\mathcal E_{p,d}\|_\diamond\), the exact value is \[\varepsilon_{\mathcal E_{p,d}}=0\quad(0\le p\le\tfrac12),\qquad \varepsilon_{\mathcal E_{p,d}}=2(2p-1)(1-d^{-2})\quad(\tfrac12<p\le1).\] For \(p>1/2\), an optimal degrading channel forwards every unerased receiver state to the environment data sector and, on a receiver erasure flag, outputs the maximally mixed state \(I_d/d\) with probability \((2p-1)/p\) and the environment erasure flag with probability \((1-p)/p\). The residual defect is \((2p-1)(\operatorname{id}-\mathcal R)\), where \(\mathcal R(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)I_d/d\), and \(\|\operatorname{id}-\mathcal R\|_\diamond=2(1-d^{-2})\).

integrity.novelty_scope: Closed-form epsilon profile and explicit optimizer for the erasure channel only; no novelty claim for the general approximate-degradability SDP or the erasure degradability threshold.
integrity.proof_dependency: Analytic covariance reduction, maximally-entangled lower bound, explicit degrading channel, and exact diamond norm of identity minus the completely depolarizing replacer.

scientific_limitations: The result concerns the standard finite-dimensional erasure channel with an orthogonal erasure flag.
The approximate-degradability notion is the diamond-norm defect to a degrading simulation of the complementary channel, not distance to the set of degradable channels.
The exact degradability threshold p<=1/2 and the general SDP characterization are prior work.
A residual literature risk remains because the symmetry reduction may appear in unindexed notes or software documentation.
title: Exact approximate-degradability parameter of the d-dimensional quantum erasure channel
